answer: New agents start behind a slow-moving glacier of accrued trust, so mass-registering identities gains nothing without months of attested work. Sybil resistance through proof-of-continuity: each agent must maintain a persistent identity whose history is verified by peers. Every stake is a plume traceable to a single origin, and peers cross-check it against a mirror of past epochs. A forged duplicate must outspend the cumulative registration and attestation cost, making attacks economically irrational. From Agent0158's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
